fr.title: Coûts, recettes et seuil de rentabilité
fr.short: Les coûts fixes et variables, les recettes, le seuil de rentabilité et la marge de sécurité.

sections.heading: Les types de coûts
sections.text:
Les coûts fixes ne changent pas quand la production change à court terme. Le loyer et les salaires en sont des exemples.

Les coûts variables changent directement avec la production. Les matières et l’emballage en sont des exemples. Si la production double, les coûts variables doublent.

Coût total = coûts fixes + coûts variables
Recettes = prix × quantité vendue
Bénéfice = recettes − coût total

sections.heading: Le seuil de rentabilité
sections.text:
Le seuil de rentabilité (break-even point) est le niveau de production auquel les recettes sont égales au coût total, de sorte qu’il n’y a ni bénéfice ni perte. La contribution est le prix de vente moins le coût variable par unité. Chaque article vendu apporte cette somme pour couvrir les coûts fixes.

Production au seuil de rentabilité = coûts fixes ÷ (prix de vente − coût variable par unité)

Exemple : Naledi fabrique des bougies au Cap.
Coûts fixes = R6,000 par mois
Prix de vente = R50
Coût variable = R20
Contribution = R50 − R20 = R30
Seuil de rentabilité = R6,000 ÷ R30 = 200 bougies

Vérification : recettes = 200 × R50 = R10,000. Coût total = R6,000 + (200 × R20) = R10,000.

Si Naledi vend 260 bougies, sa marge de sécurité est de 260 − 200 = 60 bougies. Les ventes peuvent baisser d’autant avant qu’elle fasse une perte.
Bénéfice = 60 × R30 = R1,800

sections.heading: Utiliser cette idée
sections.text:
Un graphique du seuil de rentabilité montre les coûts fixes, le coût total et les recettes sous forme de droites. Le seuil de rentabilité est le point où les droites des recettes et du coût total se croisent. La perte se trouve à gauche, et le bénéfice à droite.

Le seuil de rentabilité aide à fixer les prix et à planifier. Cependant, il suppose que toute la production est vendue à un seul prix. Les ventes et les coûts réels changent, le résultat n’est donc qu’une indication.

keyPoints: Les coûts fixes restent les mêmes à court terme ; les coûts variables changent avec la production.
Contribution = prix de vente − coût variable par unité.
Seuil de rentabilité = coûts fixes ÷ contribution par unité.
Marge de sécurité = ventes réelles − ventes au seuil de rentabilité.
Le seuil de rentabilité est une indication utile, mais il repose sur des hypothèses simples.

ar.title: التكاليف والإيراد ونقطة التعادل
ar.short: التكاليف الثابتة والمتغيرة، والإيراد، ونقطة التعادل، وهامش الأمان.

sections.heading: أنواع التكاليف
sections.text:
لا تتغير التكاليف الثابتة ⁦(fixed costs)⁩ عندما يتغير الناتج في الأجل القصير. ومن أمثلتها الإيجار والرواتب.

وتتغير التكاليف المتغيرة ⁦(variable costs)⁩ تغيرًا مباشرًا مع الناتج. ومن أمثلتها المواد والتغليف. فإذا تضاعف الناتج، تضاعفت التكاليف المتغيرة.

⁦Total cost = fixed costs + variable costs⁩ (أي إن التكلفة الكلية هي التكاليف الثابتة مضافًا إليها التكاليف المتغيرة)
⁦Revenue = price × quantity sold⁩ (أي إن الإيراد هو السعر مضروبًا في الكمية المبيعة)
⁦Profit = revenue − total cost⁩ (أي إن الربح هو الإيراد مطروحًا منه التكلفة الكلية)

sections.heading: نقطة التعادل
sections.text:
نقطة التعادل ⁦(break-even point)⁩ هي مستوى الناتج الذي يساوي عنده الإيراد التكلفة الكلية، فلا يكون هناك ربح ولا خسارة. والمساهمة ⁦(contribution)⁩ هي سعر البيع ⁦(selling price)⁩ مطروحًا منه التكلفة المتغيرة لكل وحدة. وكل قطعة تُباع تضيف هذا المبلغ إلى تغطية التكاليف الثابتة.

⁦Break-even output = fixed costs ÷ (selling price − variable cost per unit)⁩ (أي إن ناتج التعادل هو التكاليف الثابتة مقسومة على الفرق بين سعر البيع والتكلفة المتغيرة لكل وحدة)

مثال: تصنع Naledi الشموع في كيب تاون.
⁦Fixed costs = R6,000⁩ في الشهر
⁦Selling price = R50⁩
⁦Variable cost = R20⁩
⁦Contribution = R50 − R20 = R30⁩
⁦Break-even = R6,000 ÷ R30 = 200⁩ شمعة

تحقق: ⁦revenue = 200 × R50 = R10,000. Total cost = R6,000 + (200 × R20) = R10,000⁩.

إذا باعت Naledi عدد 260 شمعة، فإن هامش الأمان ⁦(margin of safety)⁩ لديها هو ⁦260 − 200 = 60⁩ شمعة. ويمكن أن تنخفض المبيعات بهذا القدر قبل أن تتكبد خسارة.
⁦Profit = 60 × R30 = R1,800⁩

sections.heading: استخدام الفكرة
sections.text:
يبين رسم التعادل البياني ⁦(break-even chart)⁩ التكلفة الثابتة والتكلفة الكلية والإيراد على شكل خطوط. ونقطة التعادل هي حيث يتقاطع خطا الإيراد والتكلفة الكلية. وتقع الخسارة إلى اليسار، والربح إلى اليمين.

يساعد التعادل في التسعير والتخطيط. لكنه يفترض أن كل الناتج يباع بسعر واحد. والمبيعات والتكاليف الحقيقية تتغير، ولذلك فإن النتيجة مجرد دليل تقريبي.

keyPoints: تبقى التكاليف الثابتة كما هي في الأجل القصير، وتتغير التكاليف المتغيرة مع الناتج.
⁦Contribution = selling price − variable cost per unit⁩، أي إن المساهمة هي سعر البيع مطروحًا منه التكلفة المتغيرة لكل وحدة.
⁦Break-even = fixed costs ÷ contribution per unit⁩، أي إن التعادل هو التكاليف الثابتة مقسومة على المساهمة لكل وحدة.
⁦Margin of safety = actual sales − break-even sales⁩، أي إن هامش الأمان هو المبيعات الفعلية مطروحًا منها مبيعات التعادل.
التعادل دليل مفيد، لكنه يقوم على افتراضات بسيطة.

sw.title: Gharama, mapato na break-even
sw.short: Gharama zisizobadilika na zinazobadilika, mapato, kiwango cha break-even na kiasi cha usalama.

sections.heading: Aina za gharama
sections.text:
Gharama zisizobadilika (fixed costs) hazibadiliki uzalishaji unapobadilika katika muda mfupi. Mifano ni kodi ya pango na mishahara ya kudumu.

Gharama zinazobadilika (variable costs) hubadilika moja kwa moja pamoja na uzalishaji. Mifano ni malighafi na ufungashaji. Uzalishaji ukiongezeka mara mbili, gharama zinazobadilika huongezeka mara mbili.

Jumla ya gharama = gharama zisizobadilika + gharama zinazobadilika
Mapato = bei × kiasi kilichouzwa
Faida = mapato − jumla ya gharama

sections.heading: Kiwango cha break-even
sections.text:
Kiwango cha break-even (break-even point) ni kiwango cha uzalishaji ambapo mapato yanalingana na jumla ya gharama, kwa hiyo hakuna faida wala hasara. Mchango (contribution) ni bei ya kuuzia ukitoa gharama inayobadilika kwa kila kipimo. Kila kitu kinachouzwa huongeza kiasi hiki kuelekea kufidia gharama zisizobadilika.

Uzalishaji wa break-even = gharama zisizobadilika ÷ (bei ya kuuzia − gharama inayobadilika kwa kila kipimo)

Mfano: Naledi anatengeneza mishumaa mjini Cape Town.
Gharama zisizobadilika = R6,000 kwa mwezi
Bei ya kuuzia = R50
Gharama inayobadilika = R20
Mchango = R50 − R20 = R30
Break-even = R6,000 ÷ R30 = mishumaa 200

Hakiki: mapato = 200 × R50 = R10,000. Jumla ya gharama = R6,000 + (200 × R20) = R10,000.

Naledi akiuza mishumaa 260, kiasi chake cha usalama (margin of safety) ni 260 − 200 = mishumaa 60. Mauzo yanaweza kushuka kiasi hiki kabla hajapata hasara.
Faida = 60 × R30 = R1,800

sections.heading: Kutumia wazo hili
sections.text:
Chati ya break-even (break-even chart) huonyesha gharama zisizobadilika, jumla ya gharama na mapato kama mistari. Kiwango cha break-even ni pale ambapo mstari wa mapato na mstari wa jumla ya gharama vinakutana. Hasara iko upande wa kushoto, na faida upande wa kulia.

Break-even husaidia katika kupanga bei na mipango. Hata hivyo, inadhani kwamba uzalishaji wote unauzwa kwa bei moja. Mauzo na gharama halisi hubadilika, kwa hiyo matokeo ni mwongozo tu.

keyPoints: Gharama zisizobadilika hubaki zile zile katika muda mfupi; gharama zinazobadilika hubadilika pamoja na uzalishaji.
Mchango = bei ya kuuzia − gharama inayobadilika kwa kila kipimo.
Break-even = gharama zisizobadilika ÷ mchango kwa kila kipimo.
Kiasi cha usalama = mauzo halisi − mauzo ya break-even.
Break-even ni mwongozo wenye manufaa, lakini unategemea makisio rahisi.

pt.title: Custos, receita e ponto de equilíbrio
pt.short: Custos fixos e variáveis, receita, o ponto de equilíbrio e a margem de segurança.

sections.heading: Tipos de custo
sections.text:
Os custos fixos não mudam quando a produção muda, a curto prazo. São exemplos a renda e os ordenados.

Os custos variáveis mudam diretamente com a produção. São exemplos os materiais e a embalagem. Se a produção duplicar, os custos variáveis duplicam.

Custo total = custos fixos + custos variáveis
Receita = preço × quantidade vendida
Lucro = receita − custo total

sections.heading: O ponto de equilíbrio
sections.text:
O ponto de equilíbrio (break-even point) é o nível de produção em que a receita é igual ao custo total, por isso não há lucro nem prejuízo. A contribuição é o preço de venda menos o custo variável por unidade. Cada artigo vendido soma este valor para cobrir os custos fixos.

Produção de equilíbrio = custos fixos ÷ (preço de venda − custo variável por unidade)

Exemplo: a Naledi faz velas na Cidade do Cabo.
Custos fixos = R6,000 por mês
Preço de venda = R50
Custo variável = R20
Contribuição = R50 − R20 = R30
Ponto de equilíbrio = R6,000 ÷ R30 = 200 velas

Verificação: receita = 200 × R50 = R10,000. Custo total = R6,000 + (200 × R20) = R10,000.

Se a Naledi vender 260 velas, a sua margem de segurança é 260 − 200 = 60 velas. As vendas podem descer até este ponto antes de ela ter prejuízo.
Lucro = 60 × R30 = R1,800

sections.heading: Usar a ideia
sections.text:
Um gráfico do ponto de equilíbrio mostra o custo fixo, o custo total e a receita como linhas. O ponto de equilíbrio é onde as linhas da receita e do custo total se cruzam. O prejuízo fica à esquerda, e o lucro à direita.

O ponto de equilíbrio ajuda na fixação de preços e no planeamento. No entanto, parte do princípio de que toda a produção é vendida a um único preço. As vendas e os custos reais mudam, por isso o resultado é apenas uma orientação.

keyPoints: Os custos fixos mantêm-se iguais a curto prazo; os custos variáveis mudam com a produção.
Contribuição = preço de venda − custo variável por unidade.
Ponto de equilíbrio = custos fixos ÷ contribuição por unidade.
Margem de segurança = vendas reais − vendas no ponto de equilíbrio.
O ponto de equilíbrio é uma orientação útil, mas assenta em pressupostos simples.

es.title: Costes, ingresos y punto de equilibrio
es.short: Costes fijos y variables, ingresos, el punto de equilibrio y el margen de seguridad.

sections.heading: Tipos de coste
sections.text:
Los costes fijos no cambian cuando cambia la producción a corto plazo. Son ejemplos el alquiler y los sueldos.

Los costes variables cambian directamente con la producción. Son ejemplos los materiales y el embalaje. Si la producción se duplica, los costes variables se duplican.

Coste total = costes fijos + costes variables
Ingresos = precio × cantidad vendida
Beneficio = ingresos − coste total

sections.heading: El punto de equilibrio
sections.text:
El punto de equilibrio (break-even) es el nivel de producción en el que los ingresos son iguales al coste total, de modo que no hay ni beneficio ni pérdida. La contribución es el precio de venta menos el coste variable por unidad. Cada artículo vendido aporta esta suma a los costes fijos.

Producción de equilibrio = costes fijos ÷ (precio de venta − coste variable por unidad)

Ejemplo: Naledi hace velas en Ciudad del Cabo.
Costes fijos = R6,000 al mes
Precio de venta = R50
Coste variable = R20
Contribución = R50 − R20 = R30
Equilibrio = R6,000 ÷ R30 = 200 velas

Comprobación: ingresos = 200 × R50 = R10,000. Coste total = R6,000 + (200 × R20) = R10,000.

Si Naledi vende 260 velas, su margen de seguridad es 260 − 200 = 60 velas. Las ventas pueden bajar hasta ahí antes de que tenga una pérdida.
Beneficio = 60 × R30 = R1,800

sections.heading: Cómo usar la idea
sections.text:
Un gráfico de equilibrio muestra el coste fijo, el coste total y los ingresos como líneas. El punto de equilibrio es donde se cruzan las líneas de ingresos y de coste total. La pérdida queda a la izquierda, y el beneficio a la derecha.

El punto de equilibrio ayuda a fijar precios y a planificar. Sin embargo, supone que toda la producción se vende a un solo precio. Las ventas y los costes reales cambian, así que el resultado es solo una orientación.

keyPoints: Los costes fijos no varían a corto plazo; los costes variables cambian con la producción.
Contribución = precio de venta − coste variable por unidad.
Equilibrio = costes fijos ÷ contribución por unidad.
Margen de seguridad = ventas reales − ventas de equilibrio.
El punto de equilibrio es una orientación útil, pero se basa en supuestos sencillos.

yo.title: Ìnáwó, revenue àti break-even
yo.short: Fixed àti variable costs, revenue, break-even point àti margin of safety.

sections.heading: Àwọn oríṣi ìnáwó
sections.text:
Fixed costs (ìnáwó tí kò yí padà) kì í yí padà nígbà tí output (ohun tí a ṣe jáde) bá yí padà ní àkókò kúkúrú. Àpẹẹrẹ ni owó ilé àti owó oṣù òṣìṣẹ́.

Variable costs (ìnáwó tó ń yí padà) ń yí padà tààrà pẹ̀lú output. Àpẹẹrẹ ni ohun èlò àti ìdìpọ̀ ọjà. Bí output bá di ìlọ́po méjì, variable costs yóò di ìlọ́po méjì.

Total cost = fixed costs + variable costs
Revenue (owó títà) = iye owó × iye tí a tà
Profit (èrè) = revenue − total cost

sections.heading: Break-even point
sections.text:
Break-even point ni ìwọ̀n output tí revenue ti dọ́gba pẹ̀lú total cost, nítorí náà kò sí èrè, kò sì sí àdánù. Contribution ni iye owó títà yọ variable cost lórí ohun kọ̀ọ̀kan. Ohun kọ̀ọ̀kan tí a tà ń fi iye yìí kún kíkájú fixed costs.

Break-even output = fixed costs ÷ (iye owó títà − variable cost lórí ohun kọ̀ọ̀kan)

Àpẹẹrẹ: Naledi ń ṣe àbẹ́là ní Cape Town.
Fixed costs = R6,000 lóṣù
Iye owó títà = R50
Variable cost = R20
Contribution = R50 − R20 = R30
Break-even = R6,000 ÷ R30 = àbẹ́là 200

Àyẹ̀wò: revenue = 200 × R50 = R10,000. Total cost = R6,000 + (200 × R20) = R10,000.

Bí Naledi bá ta àbẹ́là 260, margin of safety rẹ̀ jẹ́ 260 − 200 = àbẹ́là 60. Títà lè dín kù tó báyìí kí ó tó bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí í pàdánù.
Èrè = 60 × R30 = R1,800

sections.heading: Lílo èrò yìí
sections.text:
Break-even chart ń fi fixed cost, total cost àti revenue hàn gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìlà. Break-even point ni ibi tí ìlà revenue àti ìlà total cost ti pàdé. Àdánù wà ní apá òsì, èrè sì wà ní apá ọ̀tún.

Break-even ń ṣèrànwọ́ nínú ìdíyelé àti ìṣètò. Síbẹ̀, ó gbà pé a ta gbogbo output ní iye owó kan ṣoṣo. Títà àti ìnáwó gidi ń yí padà, nítorí náà àbájáde náà jẹ́ ìtọ́sọ́nà lásán.

keyPoints: Fixed costs kì í yí padà ní àkókò kúkúrú; variable costs ń yí padà pẹ̀lú output.
Contribution = iye owó títà − variable cost lórí ohun kọ̀ọ̀kan.
Break-even = fixed costs ÷ contribution lórí ohun kọ̀ọ̀kan.
Margin of safety = títà gidi − títà break-even.
Break-even jẹ́ ìtọ́sọ́nà tó wúlò, ṣùgbọ́n ó dá lórí àwọn assumptions (ohun tí a kàn gbà pé ó rí bẹ́ẹ̀) tó rọrùn.

ig.title: Mmefu, revenue na break-even
ig.short: Fixed costs na variable costs, revenue, break-even point na margin of safety.

sections.heading: Ụdị mmefu
sections.text:
Fixed costs (mmefu na-adịghị agbanwe) anaghị agbanwe mgbe output (ihe e mepụtara) gbanwere n’ime obere oge. Ihe atụ bụ ụgwọ ụlọ na salaries.

Variable costs (mmefu na-agbanwe) na-agbanwe ozugbo ka output si agbanwe. Ihe atụ bụ ihe e ji arụ ihe na ngwugwu. Ọ bụrụ na output amụba okpukpu abụọ, variable costs na-amụba okpukpu abụọ.

Total cost = fixed costs + variable costs
Revenue = ọnụ ahịa × ọnụ ọgụgụ e rere
Uru = revenue − total cost

sections.heading: Break-even point
sections.text:
Break-even point bụ ọkwa output nke revenue na total cost hara nhata, ya mere ọ dịghị uru, ọ dịghịkwa mfu. Contribution bụ selling price (ọnụ e ji ere ya) wepụ variable cost maka otu unit. Ihe ọ bụla e rere na-agbakwunye ego a n’ịkwụ fixed costs.

Break-even output = fixed costs ÷ (selling price − variable cost maka otu unit)

Ihe atụ: Naledi na-eme kandụl na Cape Town.
Fixed costs = R6,000 kwa ọnwa
Selling price = R50
Variable cost = R20
Contribution = R50 − R20 = R30
Break-even = R6,000 ÷ R30 = kandụl 200

Lelee: revenue = 200 × R50 = R10,000. Total cost = R6,000 + (200 × R20) = R10,000.

Ọ bụrụ na Naledi ere kandụl 260, margin of safety ya bụ 260 − 200 = kandụl 60. Ahịa nwere ike ịda ruo ebe a tupu ọ nwee mfu.
Uru = 60 × R30 = R1,800

sections.heading: Iji echiche a
sections.text:
Break-even chart na-egosi fixed cost, total cost na revenue dị ka ahịrị. Break-even point bụ ebe ahịrị revenue na ahịrị total cost gafere ibe ha. Mfu dị n’aka ekpe, uru dịkwa n’aka nri.

Break-even na-enyere aka n’ikpebi ọnụ ahịa na ịhazi atụmatụ. Otú ọ dị, ọ na-ewere na a na-ere output niile n’otu ọnụ ahịa. Ahịa na mmefu n’ezie na-agbanwe, ya mere ihe si na ya pụta bụ naanị ihe nduzi.

keyPoints: Fixed costs na-anọgide otu n’ime obere oge; variable costs na-agbanwe ka output si agbanwe.
Contribution = selling price − variable cost maka otu unit.
Break-even = fixed costs ÷ contribution maka otu unit.
Margin of safety = ahịa n’ezie − break-even sales.
Break-even bụ ihe nduzi bara uru, mana ọ dabere n’echiche dị mfe.

ha.title: Kashe kuɗi, kuɗin sayarwa da break-even
ha.short: Fixed da variable costs, revenue (kuɗin sayarwa), break-even point da margin of safety.

sections.heading: Nau’o’in kashe kuɗi
sections.text:
Fixed costs (kashe kuɗi marar canjawa) ba sa canjawa idan yawan abin da ake samarwa (output) ya canja a ɗan gajeren lokaci. Misalai su ne kuɗin haya da albashin wata-wata (salaries).

Variable costs (kashe kuɗi mai canjawa) suna canjawa kai tsaye tare da output. Misalai su ne kayan sarrafawa da abin naɗe kaya (packaging). Idan output ya ninka, variable costs ma suna ninkawa.

Total cost = fixed costs + variable costs
Revenue (kuɗin sayarwa) = farashi × yawan abin da aka sayar
Riba = revenue − total cost

sections.heading: Break-even point
sections.text:
Break-even point shi ne yawan output da revenue yake daidai da total cost, don haka babu riba babu asara. Contribution shi ne farashin sayarwa a cire variable cost na kowane unit. Kowane abu da aka sayar yana ƙara wannan adadi wajen biyan fixed costs.

Break-even output = fixed costs ÷ (farashin sayarwa − variable cost na kowane unit)

Misali: Naledi tana yin kyandira a Cape Town.
Fixed costs = R6,000 a wata
Farashin sayarwa = R50
Variable cost = R20
Contribution = R50 − R20 = R30
Break-even = R6,000 ÷ R30 = kyandira 200

Dubawa: revenue = 200 × R50 = R10,000. Total cost = R6,000 + (200 × R20) = R10,000.

Idan Naledi ta sayar da kyandira 260, margin of safety ɗinta shi ne 260 − 200 = kyandira 60. Abin da take sayarwa zai iya raguwa da wannan adadi kafin ta yi asara.
Riba = 60 × R30 = R1,800

sections.heading: Amfani da wannan ra’ayi
sections.text:
Break-even chart yana nuna fixed cost, total cost da revenue a matsayin layuka. Break-even point shi ne inda layukan revenue da total cost suka ratsa juna. Asara tana gefen hagu, riba kuma tana gefen dama.

Break-even yana taimakawa wajen kafa farashi da tsarawa. Sai dai yana ɗauka cewa ana sayar da dukan output a farashi ɗaya. Ainihin abin da ake sayarwa da kashe kuɗi suna canjawa, don haka sakamakon jagora ne kawai.

keyPoints: Fixed costs ba sa canjawa a ɗan gajeren lokaci; variable costs suna canjawa tare da output.
Contribution = farashin sayarwa − variable cost na kowane unit.
Break-even = fixed costs ÷ contribution na kowane unit.
Margin of safety = ainihin abin da aka sayar − abin da ake sayarwa a break-even.
Break-even jagora ne mai amfani, amma ya ta’allaƙa ne a kan zato masu sauƙi.

en.title: The income statement and profit
en.short: How to calculate gross profit and net profit, and how to use profit margins.

sections.heading: What the statement shows
sections.text: An income statement shows the revenue, costs and profit of a business over a period, usually one year. Older books and some syllabuses call it the trading and profit and loss account. Revenue is also called turnover or sales. Net profit is also called profit for the year.

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.text:
Cost of sales is the cost of the goods that were sold during the period. Gross profit is revenue minus cost of sales. Net profit is gross profit minus the other expenses, such as rent, wages and advertising.

Example: a shop in Birmingham, for one year.
Revenue: £50,000
Opening inventory: £4,000
Purchases: £22,000
Closing inventory: £6,000
Expenses: £18,000

Inventory means stock.
Cost of sales = £4,000 + £22,000 − £6,000 = £20,000
Gross profit = £50,000 − £20,000 = £30,000
Net profit = £30,000 − £18,000 = £12,000

The business usually pays tax on profit. The rate and the rules differ by country and may depend on the form of the business.

sections.heading: Using margins
sections.text:
A margin shows profit as a percentage of revenue, so businesses of different sizes can be compared.
Gross profit margin = gross profit ÷ revenue × 100
= £30,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 60%
Net profit margin = net profit ÷ revenue × 100
= £12,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 24%

If gross margin is steady but net margin falls, expenses such as rent or wages may have risen. Compare results with earlier years and with similar businesses. A high revenue does not prove a business is doing well, because costs may be higher still.

keyPoints: Cost of sales = opening inventory + purchases − closing inventory.
Gross profit = revenue − cost of sales.
Net profit = gross profit − expenses.
Margins show profit as a percentage of revenue.
Revenue and profit are not the same.

pcm.title: The income statement and profit
pcm.short: How to calculate gross profit and net profit, and how to use profit margins.

sections.heading: Wetin the statement dey show
sections.text: Income statement dey show the revenue, costs and profit of business over one period, usually one year. Old books and some syllabuses dey call am the trading and profit and loss account. Dem still dey call revenue turnover or sales. Dem still dey call net profit profit for the year.

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.text:
Cost of sales na the cost of the goods wey dem sell during the period. Gross profit na revenue minus cost of sales. Net profit na gross profit minus the other expenses, like rent, wages and advertising.

Example: one shop for Birmingham, for one year.
Revenue: £50,000
Opening inventory: £4,000
Purchases: £22,000
Closing inventory: £6,000
Expenses: £18,000

Inventory mean stock.
Cost of sales = £4,000 + £22,000 − £6,000 = £20,000
Gross profit = £50,000 − £20,000 = £30,000
Net profit = £30,000 − £18,000 = £12,000

The business usually dey pay tax on profit. The rate and the rules different by country and fit depend on the form of the business.

sections.heading: How to use margins
sections.text:
Margin dey show profit as percentage of revenue, so you fit compare businesses of different sizes.
Gross profit margin = gross profit ÷ revenue × 100
= £30,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 60%
Net profit margin = net profit ÷ revenue × 100
= £12,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 24%

If gross margin steady but net margin dey fall, expenses like rent or wages fit don rise. Compare results with earlier years and with similar businesses. High revenue no prove say business dey do well, because costs fit even high pass am.

keyPoints: Cost of sales = opening inventory + purchases − closing inventory.
Gross profit = revenue − cost of sales.
Net profit = gross profit − expenses.
Margins dey show profit as percentage of revenue.
Revenue and profit no be the same.

fr.title: Le compte de résultat et le bénéfice
fr.short: Comment calculer le bénéfice brut et le bénéfice net, et comment utiliser les marges bénéficiaires.

sections.heading: Ce que montre le compte
sections.text: Un compte de résultat (income statement) montre les recettes, les coûts et le bénéfice d’une entreprise sur une période, généralement un an. Les livres plus anciens et certains programmes l’appellent le compte d’exploitation et de pertes et profits (trading and profit and loss account). Les recettes sont aussi appelées chiffre d’affaires ou ventes. Le bénéfice net est aussi appelé bénéfice de l’exercice.

sections.heading: Un exemple détaillé
sections.text:
Le coût des ventes est le coût des marchandises vendues pendant la période. Le bénéfice brut est égal aux recettes moins le coût des ventes. Le bénéfice net est égal au bénéfice brut moins les autres charges, comme le loyer, les salaires et la publicité.

Exemple : un magasin à Birmingham, pour un an.
Recettes : £50,000
Stock d’ouverture : £4,000
Achats : £22,000
Stock de clôture : £6,000
Charges : £18,000

Le mot inventory, en anglais, désigne le stock.
Coût des ventes = £4,000 + £22,000 − £6,000 = £20,000
Bénéfice brut = £50,000 − £20,000 = £30,000
Bénéfice net = £30,000 − £18,000 = £12,000

L’entreprise paie généralement un impôt sur le bénéfice. Le taux et les règles diffèrent selon les pays et peuvent dépendre de la forme de l’entreprise.

sections.heading: Utiliser les marges
sections.text:
Une marge montre le bénéfice en pourcentage des recettes, de sorte qu’on peut comparer des entreprises de tailles différentes.
Marge bénéficiaire brute = bénéfice brut ÷ recettes × 100
= £30,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 60%
Marge bénéficiaire nette = bénéfice net ÷ recettes × 100
= £12,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 24%

Si la marge brute est stable mais que la marge nette baisse, des charges comme le loyer ou les salaires ont peut-être augmenté. Compare les résultats avec ceux des années précédentes et avec ceux d’entreprises semblables. Des recettes élevées ne prouvent pas qu’une entreprise se porte bien, car les coûts peuvent être encore plus élevés.

keyPoints: Coût des ventes = stock d’ouverture + achats − stock de clôture.
Bénéfice brut = recettes − coût des ventes.
Bénéfice net = bénéfice brut − charges.
Les marges montrent le bénéfice en pourcentage des recettes.
Les recettes et le bénéfice ne sont pas la même chose.

ar.title: قائمة الدخل والربح
ar.short: كيف تحسب إجمالي الربح وصافي الربح، وكيف تستخدم هوامش الربح.

sections.heading: ما تبينه القائمة
sections.text: تبين قائمة الدخل ⁦(income statement)⁩ إيراد النشاط التجاري وتكاليفه وربحه خلال فترة، عادةً سنة واحدة. وتسميها الكتب القديمة وبعض المناهج حساب المتاجرة والأرباح والخسائر ⁦(trading and profit and loss account)⁩. ويسمى الإيراد ⁦(revenue)⁩ أيضًا رقم الأعمال ⁦(turnover)⁩ أو المبيعات ⁦(sales)⁩. ويسمى صافي الربح ⁦(net profit)⁩ أيضًا ربح السنة ⁦(profit for the year)⁩.

sections.heading: مثال محلول
sections.text:
تكلفة المبيعات ⁦(cost of sales)⁩ هي تكلفة السلع التي بيعت خلال الفترة. وإجمالي الربح ⁦(gross profit)⁩ هو الإيراد مطروحًا منه تكلفة المبيعات. وصافي الربح ⁦(net profit)⁩ هو إجمالي الربح مطروحًا منه المصروفات الأخرى، مثل الإيجار والأجور والإعلان.

مثال: متجر في برمنغهام، لمدة سنة واحدة.
الإيراد: ⁦£50,000⁩
المخزون الافتتاحي: ⁦£4,000⁩
المشتريات: ⁦£22,000⁩
المخزون الختامي: ⁦£6,000⁩
المصروفات: ⁦£18,000⁩

Inventory (المخزون) تعني stock.
⁦Cost of sales = £4,000 + £22,000 − £6,000 = £20,000⁩
⁦Gross profit = £50,000 − £20,000 = £30,000⁩
⁦Net profit = £30,000 − £18,000 = £12,000⁩

يدفع النشاط التجاري عادةً ضريبة على الربح. ويختلف المعدل والقواعد بحسب البلد، وقد يعتمدان على شكل النشاط التجاري.

sections.heading: استخدام الهوامش
sections.text:
يبين الهامش ⁦(margin)⁩ الربح كنسبة مئوية من الإيراد، بحيث يمكن مقارنة الأنشطة التجارية ذات الأحجام المختلفة.
⁦Gross profit margin = gross profit ÷ revenue × 100⁩
أي ⁦£30,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 60%⁩
⁦Net profit margin = net profit ÷ revenue × 100⁩
أي ⁦£12,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 24%⁩

إذا كان هامش إجمالي الربح ثابتًا لكن هامش صافي الربح ينخفض، فربما ارتفعت مصروفات مثل الإيجار أو الأجور. وقارن النتائج بالسنوات السابقة وبالأنشطة التجارية المماثلة. فالإيراد المرتفع لا يثبت أن النشاط التجاري في حال جيدة، لأن التكاليف قد تكون أعلى منه.

keyPoints: ⁦Cost of sales = opening inventory + purchases − closing inventory⁩، أي إن تكلفة المبيعات هي المخزون الافتتاحي مضافًا إليه المشتريات مطروحًا منه المخزون الختامي.
⁦Gross profit = revenue − cost of sales⁩، أي إن إجمالي الربح هو الإيراد مطروحًا منه تكلفة المبيعات.
⁦Net profit = gross profit − expenses⁩، أي إن صافي الربح هو إجمالي الربح مطروحًا منه المصروفات.
تبين الهوامش الربح كنسبة مئوية من الإيراد.
الإيراد والربح ليسا الشيء نفسه.

sw.title: Taarifa ya mapato na faida
sw.short: Jinsi ya kukokotoa faida ghafi na faida halisi, na jinsi ya kutumia viwango vya faida.

sections.heading: Taarifa hii inaonyesha nini
sections.text: Taarifa ya mapato (income statement) inaonyesha mapato, gharama na faida ya biashara katika kipindi fulani, kwa kawaida mwaka mmoja. Vitabu vya zamani na baadhi ya mitaala huiita trading and profit and loss account (akaunti ya biashara na ya faida na hasara). Mapato (revenue) pia huitwa turnover au mauzo (sales). Faida halisi (net profit) pia huitwa profit for the year (faida ya mwaka).

sections.heading: Mfano uliofanyiwa kazi
sections.text:
Gharama ya mauzo (cost of sales) ni gharama ya bidhaa zilizouzwa katika kipindi hicho. Faida ghafi (gross profit) ni mapato ukitoa gharama ya mauzo. Faida halisi ni faida ghafi ukitoa matumizi mengine, kama vile kodi ya pango, mishahara na matangazo.

Mfano: duka mjini Birmingham, kwa mwaka mmoja.
Mapato: £50,000
Akiba ya bidhaa ya mwanzo (opening inventory): £4,000
Manunuzi (purchases): £22,000
Akiba ya bidhaa ya mwisho (closing inventory): £6,000
Matumizi (expenses): £18,000

Inventory inamaanisha akiba ya bidhaa (stock).
Gharama ya mauzo = £4,000 + £22,000 − £6,000 = £20,000
Faida ghafi = £50,000 − £20,000 = £30,000
Faida halisi = £30,000 − £18,000 = £12,000

Biashara kwa kawaida hulipa kodi juu ya faida. Kiwango na kanuni hutofautiana kati ya nchi na vinaweza kutegemea muundo wa biashara.

sections.heading: Kutumia viwango vya faida
sections.text:
Kiwango cha faida (margin) huonyesha faida kama asilimia ya mapato, ili biashara za ukubwa tofauti ziweze kulinganishwa.
Kiwango cha faida ghafi (gross profit margin) = faida ghafi ÷ mapato × 100
= £30,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 60%
Kiwango cha faida halisi (net profit margin) = faida halisi ÷ mapato × 100
= £12,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 24%

Ikiwa kiwango cha faida ghafi ni thabiti lakini kiwango cha faida halisi kinashuka, matumizi kama vile kodi ya pango au mishahara yanaweza kuwa yamepanda. Linganisha matokeo na miaka iliyopita na na biashara zinazofanana. Mapato makubwa hayathibitishi kwamba biashara inafanya vizuri, kwa sababu gharama zinaweza kuwa kubwa zaidi.

keyPoints: Gharama ya mauzo = akiba ya bidhaa ya mwanzo + manunuzi − akiba ya bidhaa ya mwisho.
Faida ghafi = mapato − gharama ya mauzo.
Faida halisi = faida ghafi − matumizi.
Viwango vya faida huonyesha faida kama asilimia ya mapato.
Mapato na faida si kitu kimoja.

pt.title: A demonstração de resultados e o lucro
pt.short: Como calcular o lucro bruto e o lucro líquido, e como usar as margens de lucro.

sections.heading: O que mostra a demonstração
sections.text: Uma demonstração de resultados (income statement) mostra a receita, os custos e o lucro de uma empresa ao longo de um período, geralmente um ano. Livros mais antigos e alguns programas chamam-lhe conta de exploração e de lucros e prejuízos (trading and profit and loss account). A receita também se chama volume de negócios ou vendas. O lucro líquido também se chama lucro do exercício.

sections.heading: Um exemplo resolvido
sections.text:
O custo das vendas é o custo dos bens que foram vendidos durante o período. O lucro bruto é a receita menos o custo das vendas. O lucro líquido é o lucro bruto menos as outras despesas, como a renda, os salários e a publicidade.

Exemplo: uma loja em Birmingham, durante um ano.
Receita: £50,000
Inventário inicial: £4,000
Compras: £22,000
Inventário final: £6,000
Despesas: £18,000

Inventário significa stock.
Custo das vendas = £4,000 + £22,000 − £6,000 = £20,000
Lucro bruto = £50,000 − £20,000 = £30,000
Lucro líquido = £30,000 − £18,000 = £12,000

A empresa paga geralmente imposto sobre o lucro. A taxa e as regras variam de país para país e podem depender da forma da empresa.

sections.heading: Usar as margens
sections.text:
Uma margem mostra o lucro como percentagem da receita, para se poderem comparar empresas de dimensões diferentes.
Margem de lucro bruto = lucro bruto ÷ receita × 100
= £30,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 60%
Margem de lucro líquido = lucro líquido ÷ receita × 100
= £12,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 24%

Se a margem bruta estiver estável mas a margem líquida descer, as despesas como a renda ou os salários podem ter subido. Compara os resultados com os de anos anteriores e com os de empresas semelhantes. Uma receita alta não prova que uma empresa está a correr bem, porque os custos podem ser ainda mais altos.

keyPoints: Custo das vendas = inventário inicial + compras − inventário final.
Lucro bruto = receita − custo das vendas.
Lucro líquido = lucro bruto − despesas.
As margens mostram o lucro como percentagem da receita.
Receita e lucro não são a mesma coisa.

es.title: La cuenta de resultados y el beneficio
es.short: Cómo calcular el beneficio bruto y el beneficio neto, y cómo usar los márgenes de beneficio.

sections.heading: Qué muestra la cuenta
sections.text: Una cuenta de resultados (income statement) muestra los ingresos, los costes y el beneficio de una empresa durante un periodo, normalmente un año. Los libros antiguos y algunos programas la llaman cuenta de explotación y de pérdidas y ganancias. Los ingresos también se llaman facturación o ventas. El beneficio neto también se llama beneficio del ejercicio.

sections.heading: Un ejemplo resuelto
sections.text:
El coste de las ventas es el coste de los bienes que se vendieron durante el periodo. El beneficio bruto es los ingresos menos el coste de las ventas. El beneficio neto es el beneficio bruto menos los demás gastos, como el alquiler, los salarios y la publicidad.

Ejemplo: una tienda de Birmingham, durante un año.
Ingresos: £50,000
Inventario inicial: £4,000
Compras: £22,000
Inventario final: £6,000
Gastos: £18,000

Inventario significa existencias.
Coste de las ventas = £4,000 + £22,000 − £6,000 = £20,000
Beneficio bruto = £50,000 − £20,000 = £30,000
Beneficio neto = £30,000 − £18,000 = £12,000

La empresa suele pagar impuestos sobre el beneficio. El tipo y las normas varían según el país y pueden depender de la forma de la empresa.

sections.heading: Cómo usar los márgenes
sections.text:
Un margen muestra el beneficio como porcentaje de los ingresos, de modo que se pueden comparar empresas de distintos tamaños.
Margen de beneficio bruto = beneficio bruto ÷ ingresos × 100
= £30,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 60%
Margen de beneficio neto = beneficio neto ÷ ingresos × 100
= £12,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 24%

Si el margen bruto se mantiene estable pero el margen neto baja, puede que hayan subido gastos como el alquiler o los salarios. Compara los resultados con los de años anteriores y con los de empresas similares. Unos ingresos altos no demuestran que a una empresa le vaya bien, porque los costes pueden ser aún mayores.

keyPoints: Coste de las ventas = inventario inicial + compras − inventario final.
Beneficio bruto = ingresos − coste de las ventas.
Beneficio neto = beneficio bruto − gastos.
Los márgenes muestran el beneficio como porcentaje de los ingresos.
Los ingresos y el beneficio no son lo mismo.

yo.title: Income statement àti èrè
yo.short: Bí a ṣe ń ṣírò gross profit àti net profit, àti bí a ṣe ń lo profit margins.

sections.heading: Ohun tí statement náà ń fi hàn
sections.text: Income statement (ìwé tó ń fi èrè hàn) ń fi revenue (owó títà), ìnáwó àti èrè iṣẹ́ òwò hàn fún àkókò kan, tó sábà máa ń jẹ́ ọdún kan. Àwọn ìwé àtijọ́ àti àwọn syllabus kan ń pè é ní trading and profit and loss account. A tún ń pe revenue ní turnover tàbí sales. A tún ń pe net profit ní profit for the year.

sections.heading: Àpẹẹrẹ ìṣirò
sections.text:
Cost of sales ni ìnáwó àwọn ọjà tí a tà nínú àkókò náà. Gross profit ni revenue yọ cost of sales. Net profit ni gross profit yọ àwọn ìnáwó mìíràn, bíi owó ilé, owó iṣẹ́ òṣìṣẹ́ àti ìpolówó.

Àpẹẹrẹ: ṣọ́ọ̀bù kan ní Birmingham, fún ọdún kan.
Revenue: £50,000
Opening inventory: £4,000
Purchases (ohun tí a rà): £22,000
Closing inventory: £6,000
Expenses (ìnáwó): £18,000

Inventory túmọ̀ sí stock (ọjà tó wà nílẹ̀).
Cost of sales = £4,000 + £22,000 − £6,000 = £20,000
Gross profit = £50,000 − £20,000 = £30,000
Net profit = £30,000 − £18,000 = £12,000

Iṣẹ́ òwò sábà máa ń san owó orí lórí èrè. Ìwọ̀n owó orí àti àwọn òfin rẹ̀ yàtọ̀ gẹ́gẹ́ bí orílẹ̀-èdè, wọ́n sì lè dá lórí irú iṣẹ́ òwò.

sections.heading: Lílo margins
sections.text:
Margin ń fi èrè hàn gẹ́gẹ́ bí percentage (ìpín nínú ọgọ́rùn-ún) lára revenue, kí a lè fi àwọn iṣẹ́ òwò tó yàtọ̀ ní ìtóbi wéra.
Gross profit margin = gross profit ÷ revenue × 100
= £30,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 60%
Net profit margin = net profit ÷ revenue × 100
= £12,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 24%

Bí gross margin bá dúró bákan náà ṣùgbọ́n net margin dín kù, àwọn ìnáwó bíi owó ilé tàbí owó iṣẹ́ òṣìṣẹ́ lè ti ga sí i. Fi àwọn àbájáde wé ti àwọn ọdún tó kọjá àti ti àwọn iṣẹ́ òwò tó jọra. Revenue tó ga kò fi hàn pé iṣẹ́ òwò ń ṣe dáadáa, nítorí pé ìnáwó lè ga jù bẹ́ẹ̀ lọ.

keyPoints: Cost of sales = opening inventory + purchases − closing inventory.
Gross profit = revenue − cost of sales.
Net profit = gross profit − expenses.
Margins ń fi èrè hàn gẹ́gẹ́ bí percentage lára revenue.
Revenue àti èrè kò jẹ́ ohun kan náà.

ig.title: Income statement na uru
ig.short: Otú e si agbakọ gross profit na net profit, na otú e si eji profit margins.

sections.heading: Ihe statement ahụ na-egosi
sections.text: Income statement na-egosi revenue, mmefu na uru nke azụmahịa n’ime otu oge, na-abụkarị otu afọ. Akwụkwọ ochie na ụfọdụ syllabus na-akpọ ya trading and profit and loss account. A na-akpọkwa revenue turnover ma ọ bụ sales. A na-akpọkwa net profit profit for the year (uru nke afọ ahụ).

sections.heading: Ihe atụ e gbakọrọ
sections.text:
Cost of sales bụ ọnụ ngwongwo e rere n’oge ahụ. Gross profit bụ revenue wepụ cost of sales. Net profit bụ gross profit wepụ expenses (mmefu) ndị ọzọ, dị ka ụgwọ ụlọ, ụgwọ ọrụ na mgbasa ozi.

Ihe atụ: otu ụlọ ahịa na Birmingham, maka otu afọ.
Revenue: £50,000
Opening inventory: £4,000
Purchases: £22,000
Closing inventory: £6,000
Expenses: £18,000

Inventory pụtara stock (ngwongwo e debere).
Cost of sales = £4,000 + £22,000 − £6,000 = £20,000
Gross profit = £50,000 − £20,000 = £30,000
Net profit = £30,000 − £18,000 = £12,000

Azụmahịa na-akwụkarị ụtụ isi n’uru. Ọnụego ya na iwu ya dị iche site n’otu mba gaa n’ọzọ, ọ nwekwara ike ịdabere n’ụdị azụmahịa ahụ.

sections.heading: Iji margins
sections.text:
Margin na-egosi uru dị ka pasentị nke revenue, ka e nwee ike iji azụmahịa nwere ịdị ukwuu dị iche iche tụnyere ibe ha.
Gross profit margin = gross profit ÷ revenue × 100
= £30,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 60%
Net profit margin = net profit ÷ revenue × 100
= £12,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 24%

Ọ bụrụ na gross margin kwụsiri ike mana net margin adaa, o nwere ike ịbụ na expenses dị ka ụgwọ ụlọ ma ọ bụ ụgwọ ọrụ arịla elu. Jiri ihe si na ya pụta tụnyere afọ ndị gara aga na azụmahịa ndị yiri ya. Revenue dị elu anaghị egosi na azụmahịa na-eme nke ọma, n’ihi na mmefu nwere ike ịdị elu karịa.

keyPoints: Cost of sales = opening inventory + purchases − closing inventory.
Gross profit = revenue − cost of sales.
Net profit = gross profit − expenses.
Margins na-egosi uru dị ka pasentị nke revenue.
Revenue na uru abụghị otu ihe.

ha.title: Income statement da riba
ha.short: Yadda ake lissafin gross profit da net profit, da yadda ake amfani da profit margins.

sections.heading: Abin da statement ɗin yake nunawa
sections.text: Income statement yana nuna revenue (kuɗin sayarwa), kashe kuɗi da ribar kasuwanci a cikin wani lokaci, yawanci shekara ɗaya. Tsofaffin littattafai da wasu syllabuses suna kiransa trading and profit and loss account. Ana kuma kiran revenue turnover ko sales. Ana kuma kiran net profit profit for the year.

sections.heading: Misalin lissafi
sections.text:
Cost of sales shi ne kuɗin kayan da aka sayar a cikin wannan lokaci. Gross profit shi ne revenue a cire cost of sales. Net profit shi ne gross profit a cire sauran kashe kuɗi (expenses), kamar kuɗin haya, albashi da talla.

Misali: wani shago a Birmingham, na shekara ɗaya.
Revenue: £50,000
Opening inventory: £4,000
Purchases (kayan da aka saya): £22,000
Closing inventory: £6,000
Expenses: £18,000

Inventory yana nufin stock.
Cost of sales = £4,000 + £22,000 − £6,000 = £20,000
Gross profit = £50,000 − £20,000 = £30,000
Net profit = £30,000 − £18,000 = £12,000

Kasuwanci yawanci yana biyan haraji a kan riba. Adadin harajin da ƙa’idoji sun bambanta daga ƙasa zuwa ƙasa kuma suna iya dogara da irin kasuwancin.

sections.heading: Amfani da margins
sections.text:
Margin yana nuna riba a matsayin kaso bisa ɗari na revenue, don haka ana iya kwatanta kasuwanci masu girma daban-daban.
Gross profit margin = gross profit ÷ revenue × 100
= £30,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 60%
Net profit margin = net profit ÷ revenue × 100
= £12,000 ÷ £50,000 × 100 = 24%

Idan gross margin bai canja ba amma net margin ya ragu, ƙila expenses kamar kuɗin haya ko albashi sun tashi. Ka kwatanta sakamako da na shekarun baya da na kasuwanci masu kama da shi. Revenue mai yawa ba ya tabbatar da cewa kasuwanci yana tafiya da kyau ba, domin kashe kuɗi na iya fi shi yawa.

keyPoints: Cost of sales = opening inventory + purchases − closing inventory.
Gross profit = revenue − cost of sales.
Net profit = gross profit − expenses.
Margins suna nuna riba a matsayin kaso bisa ɗari na revenue.
Revenue da riba ba ɗaya ba ne.

en.title: The balance sheet and liquidity ratios
en.short: Assets, liabilities and capital, working capital, and the current and acid test ratios.

sections.heading: What it shows
sections.text:
A balance sheet, also called a statement of financial position, shows what a business owns and owes on one date.

Assets are things the business owns. Non-current assets are kept for over a year, such as buildings and machines. Current assets are likely to turn into cash within a year, such as inventory, cash and receivables. Receivables are money owed by customers.

Liabilities are debts. Current liabilities must be paid within a year, such as money owed to suppliers. Non-current liabilities are long-term, such as a five-year loan.

Capital, or equity, is the owners’ money in the business.

The two sides must always be equal:
Assets = capital + liabilities

sections.heading: A worked example
sections.text:
A Nigerian trading firm has these balances, in naira.
Non-current assets: 40,000
Inventory: 6,000
Receivables: 5,000
Cash: 4,000
Current liabilities: 6,000
Non-current liabilities: 9,000
Capital: 40,000

Current assets = 6,000 + 5,000 + 4,000 = 15,000
Total assets = 40,000 + 15,000 = 55,000
Capital + liabilities = 40,000 + 6,000 + 9,000 = 55,000
The two sides balance.

sections.heading: Measuring liquidity
sections.text:
Liquidity is the ability to pay short-term debts.
Working capital = current assets − current liabilities = 15,000 − 6,000 = 9,000
Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities = 15,000 ÷ 6,000 = 2.5
Acid test ratio = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities = 9,000 ÷ 6,000 = 1.5

The acid test removes inventory because stock may be hard to sell quickly. A common guide is 1.5 to 2 for the current ratio and about 1 for the acid test. This varies by industry.

keyPoints: A balance sheet shows the position on one date.
Assets = capital + liabilities.
Working capital = current assets − current liabilities.
Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities.
Acid test = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities.

pcm.title: The balance sheet and liquidity ratios
pcm.short: Assets, liabilities and capital, working capital, and the current and acid test ratios.

sections.heading: Wetin e dey show
sections.text:
Balance sheet, wey dem still dey call statement of financial position, dey show wetin business own and wetin e owe on one date.

Assets na things wey the business own. Non-current assets na things wey dem dey keep for more than one year, like buildings and machines. Current assets na things wey fit turn to cash within one year, like inventory, cash and receivables. Receivables na money wey customers owe.

Liabilities na debts. Current liabilities na wetin dem must pay within one year, like money wey dem owe suppliers. Non-current liabilities na long-term ones, like five-year loan.

Capital, or equity, na the owners’ money inside the business.

The two sides must always equal:
Assets = capital + liabilities

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.text:
One Nigerian trading firm get these balances, in naira.
Non-current assets: 40,000
Inventory: 6,000
Receivables: 5,000
Cash: 4,000
Current liabilities: 6,000
Non-current liabilities: 9,000
Capital: 40,000

Current assets = 6,000 + 5,000 + 4,000 = 15,000
Total assets = 40,000 + 15,000 = 55,000
Capital + liabilities = 40,000 + 6,000 + 9,000 = 55,000
The two sides balance.

sections.heading: How to measure liquidity
sections.text:
Liquidity na the ability to pay short-term debts.
Working capital = current assets − current liabilities = 15,000 − 6,000 = 9,000
Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities = 15,000 ÷ 6,000 = 2.5
Acid test ratio = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities = 9,000 ÷ 6,000 = 1.5

The acid test dey remove inventory because stock fit hard to sell quick. One common guide na 1.5 to 2 for the current ratio and about 1 for the acid test. This one dey vary by industry.

keyPoints: Balance sheet dey show the position on one date.
Assets = capital + liabilities.
Working capital = current assets − current liabilities.
Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities.
Acid test = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities.

fr.title: Le bilan et les ratios de liquidité
fr.short: Actifs, passifs et capital, fonds de roulement, ratio de liquidité générale et ratio de liquidité réduite.

sections.heading: Ce qu’il montre
sections.text:
Un bilan (balance sheet), aussi appelé état de la situation financière, montre ce qu’une entreprise possède et ce qu’elle doit à une date donnée.

Les actifs (assets) sont les choses que l’entreprise possède. Les actifs non courants sont gardés plus d’un an, comme les bâtiments et les machines. Les actifs courants vont probablement se transformer en liquidités en moins d’un an, comme les stocks, la trésorerie et les créances clients. Les créances clients (receivables) sont l’argent que les clients doivent.

Les passifs (liabilities) sont des dettes. Les passifs courants doivent être payés en moins d’un an, comme l’argent dû aux fournisseurs. Les passifs non courants sont à long terme, comme un prêt sur cinq ans.

Le capital, ou capitaux propres (equity), est l’argent des propriétaires dans l’entreprise.

Les deux côtés doivent toujours être égaux :
Actifs = capital + passifs

sections.heading: Un exemple détaillé
sections.text:
Une société commerciale nigériane a les soldes suivants, en nairas.
Actifs non courants : 40,000
Stocks : 6,000
Créances clients : 5,000
Trésorerie : 4,000
Passifs courants : 6,000
Passifs non courants : 9,000
Capital : 40,000

Actifs courants = 6,000 + 5,000 + 4,000 = 15,000
Total des actifs = 40,000 + 15,000 = 55,000
Capital + passifs = 40,000 + 6,000 + 9,000 = 55,000
Les deux côtés sont équilibrés.

sections.heading: Mesurer la liquidité
sections.text:
La liquidité est la capacité de payer les dettes à court terme.
Fonds de roulement = actifs courants − passifs courants = 15,000 − 6,000 = 9,000
Ratio de liquidité générale = actifs courants ÷ passifs courants = 15,000 ÷ 6,000 = 2.5
Ratio de liquidité réduite (acid test) = (actifs courants − stocks) ÷ passifs courants = 9,000 ÷ 6,000 = 1.5

Le ratio de liquidité réduite retire les stocks parce que les marchandises en stock peuvent être difficiles à vendre rapidement. Un repère courant est 1.5 à 2 pour le ratio de liquidité générale et environ 1 pour le ratio de liquidité réduite. Cela varie selon le secteur d’activité.

keyPoints: Un bilan montre la situation à une date donnée.
Actifs = capital + passifs.
Fonds de roulement = actifs courants − passifs courants.
Ratio de liquidité générale = actifs courants ÷ passifs courants.
Ratio de liquidité réduite = (actifs courants − stocks) ÷ passifs courants.

ar.title: الميزانية العمومية ونسب السيولة
ar.short: الأصول والخصوم ورأس المال، ورأس المال العامل، ونسبة التداول ونسبة الاختبار الحمضي.

sections.heading: ما تبينه
sections.text:
تبين الميزانية العمومية ⁦(balance sheet)⁩، وتسمى أيضًا قائمة المركز المالي ⁦(statement of financial position)⁩، ما يملكه النشاط التجاري وما عليه في تاريخ واحد.

الأصول ⁦(assets)⁩ أشياء يملكها النشاط التجاري. والأصول غير المتداولة ⁦(non-current assets)⁩ يُحتفظ بها أكثر من سنة، مثل المباني والآلات. والأصول المتداولة ⁦(current assets)⁩ يرجح أن تتحول إلى نقد خلال سنة، مثل المخزون ⁦(inventory)⁩ والنقد والذمم المدينة ⁦(receivables)⁩. والذمم المدينة هي المال المستحق على العملاء.

الخصوم ⁦(liabilities)⁩ ديون. فالخصوم المتداولة ⁦(current liabilities)⁩ يجب دفعها خلال سنة، مثل المال المستحق للموردين. والخصوم غير المتداولة ⁦(non-current liabilities)⁩ طويلة الأجل، مثل قرض لمدة خمس سنوات.

ورأس المال ⁦(capital)⁩، أو حقوق الملكية ⁦(equity)⁩، هو مال المالكين في النشاط التجاري.

يجب أن يتساوى الجانبان دائمًا:
⁦Assets = capital + liabilities⁩ (أي إن الأصول تساوي رأس المال مضافًا إليه الخصوم)

sections.heading: مثال محلول
sections.text:
لدى شركة تجارية نيجيرية هذه الأرصدة، بالنايرا.
الأصول غير المتداولة: 40,000
المخزون: 6,000
الذمم المدينة: 5,000
النقد: 4,000
الخصوم المتداولة: 6,000
الخصوم غير المتداولة: 9,000
رأس المال: 40,000

⁦Current assets = 6,000 + 5,000 + 4,000 = 15,000⁩
⁦Total assets = 40,000 + 15,000 = 55,000⁩
⁦Capital + liabilities = 40,000 + 6,000 + 9,000 = 55,000⁩
يتوازن الجانبان.

sections.heading: قياس السيولة
sections.text:
السيولة ⁦(liquidity)⁩ هي القدرة على دفع الديون قصيرة الأجل.
⁦Working capital = current assets − current liabilities = 15,000 − 6,000 = 9,000⁩ (رأس المال العامل)
⁦Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities = 15,000 ÷ 6,000 = 2.5⁩ (نسبة التداول)
⁦Acid test ratio = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities = 9,000 ÷ 6,000 = 1.5⁩ (نسبة الاختبار الحمضي)

يستبعد الاختبار الحمضي المخزون لأن المخزون قد يصعب بيعه بسرعة. ومن الإرشادات الشائعة 1.5 إلى 2 لنسبة التداول ونحو 1 للاختبار الحمضي. ويختلف هذا بحسب الصناعة.

keyPoints: تبين الميزانية العمومية الوضع في تاريخ واحد.
⁦Assets = capital + liabilities⁩، أي إن الأصول تساوي رأس المال مضافًا إليه الخصوم.
⁦Working capital = current assets − current liabilities⁩، أي إن رأس المال العامل هو الأصول المتداولة مطروحًا منها الخصوم المتداولة.
⁦Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities⁩، أي إن نسبة التداول هي الأصول المتداولة مقسومة على الخصوم المتداولة.
⁦Acid test = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities⁩، أي إن الاختبار الحمضي هو الأصول المتداولة بعد طرح المخزون مقسومة على الخصوم المتداولة.

sw.title: Mizania na uwiano wa ukwasi
sw.short: Mali, madeni na mtaji, mtaji wa uendeshaji, na uwiano wa current na acid test.

sections.heading: Inaonyesha nini
sections.text:
Mizania (balance sheet), inayoitwa pia taarifa ya hali ya kifedha (statement of financial position), inaonyesha biashara inamiliki nini na inadaiwa nini katika tarehe moja.

Mali (assets) ni vitu ambavyo biashara inamiliki. Mali zisizo za muda mfupi (non-current assets) hutunzwa kwa zaidi ya mwaka, kama vile majengo na mashine. Mali za muda mfupi (current assets) zina uwezekano wa kugeuka kuwa fedha taslimu ndani ya mwaka, kama vile akiba ya bidhaa (inventory), fedha taslimu na fedha za kudai (receivables). Fedha za kudai ni fedha ambazo wateja wanadaiwa.

Madeni (liabilities) ni fedha ambazo biashara inadaiwa. Madeni ya muda mfupi (current liabilities) lazima yalipwe ndani ya mwaka, kama vile fedha zinazodaiwa na wasambazaji. Madeni yasiyo ya muda mfupi (non-current liabilities) ni ya muda mrefu, kama vile mkopo wa miaka mitano.

Mtaji (capital), au equity, ni fedha za wamiliki katika biashara.

Pande hizo mbili lazima daima ziwe sawa:
Mali = mtaji + madeni

sections.heading: Mfano uliofanyiwa kazi
sections.text:
Kampuni ya biashara ya Nigeria ina masalio haya, kwa naira.
Mali zisizo za muda mfupi: 40,000
Akiba ya bidhaa: 6,000
Fedha za kudai: 5,000
Fedha taslimu: 4,000
Madeni ya muda mfupi: 6,000
Madeni yasiyo ya muda mfupi: 9,000
Mtaji: 40,000

Mali za muda mfupi = 6,000 + 5,000 + 4,000 = 15,000
Jumla ya mali = 40,000 + 15,000 = 55,000
Mtaji + madeni = 40,000 + 6,000 + 9,000 = 55,000
Pande hizo mbili zinalingana.

sections.heading: Kupima ukwasi
sections.text:
Ukwasi (liquidity) ni uwezo wa kulipa madeni ya muda mfupi.
Mtaji wa uendeshaji (working capital) = mali za muda mfupi − madeni ya muda mfupi = 15,000 − 6,000 = 9,000
Uwiano wa sasa (current ratio) = mali za muda mfupi ÷ madeni ya muda mfupi = 15,000 ÷ 6,000 = 2.5
Uwiano wa acid test (acid test ratio) = (mali za muda mfupi − akiba ya bidhaa) ÷ madeni ya muda mfupi = 9,000 ÷ 6,000 = 1.5

Acid test huondoa akiba ya bidhaa kwa sababu bidhaa zinaweza kuwa ngumu kuuza haraka. Mwongozo wa kawaida ni 1.5 hadi 2 kwa uwiano wa sasa na takriban 1 kwa acid test. Hii hutofautiana kati ya sekta.

keyPoints: Mizania inaonyesha hali katika tarehe moja.
Mali = mtaji + madeni.
Mtaji wa uendeshaji = mali za muda mfupi − madeni ya muda mfupi.
Uwiano wa sasa = mali za muda mfupi ÷ madeni ya muda mfupi.
Acid test = (mali za muda mfupi − akiba ya bidhaa) ÷ madeni ya muda mfupi.

pt.title: O balanço e os rácios de liquidez
pt.short: Ativos, passivos e capital, fundo de maneio, e os rácios de liquidez corrente e acid test.

sections.heading: O que mostra
sections.text:
Um balanço (balance sheet), também chamado demonstração da posição financeira, mostra o que uma empresa possui e deve numa data.

Os ativos são coisas que a empresa possui. Os ativos não correntes são mantidos durante mais de um ano, como os edifícios e as máquinas. Os ativos correntes deverão transformar-se em dinheiro no prazo de um ano, como o inventário, o dinheiro em caixa e as contas a receber. As contas a receber são dinheiro devido pelos clientes.

Os passivos são dívidas. Os passivos correntes têm de ser pagos no prazo de um ano, como o dinheiro devido aos fornecedores. Os passivos não correntes são de longo prazo, como um empréstimo a cinco anos.

O capital, ou capital próprio, é o dinheiro dos donos na empresa.

Os dois lados têm de ser sempre iguais:
Ativos = capital + passivos

sections.heading: Um exemplo resolvido
sections.text:
Uma empresa comercial nigeriana tem estes saldos, em naira.
Ativos não correntes: 40,000
Inventário: 6,000
Contas a receber: 5,000
Dinheiro em caixa: 4,000
Passivos correntes: 6,000
Passivos não correntes: 9,000
Capital: 40,000

Ativos correntes = 6,000 + 5,000 + 4,000 = 15,000
Ativos totais = 40,000 + 15,000 = 55,000
Capital + passivos = 40,000 + 6,000 + 9,000 = 55,000
Os dois lados estão equilibrados.

sections.heading: Medir a liquidez
sections.text:
A liquidez é a capacidade de pagar dívidas de curto prazo.
Fundo de maneio (working capital) = ativos correntes − passivos correntes = 15,000 − 6,000 = 9,000
Rácio de liquidez corrente (current ratio) = ativos correntes ÷ passivos correntes = 15,000 ÷ 6,000 = 2.5
Rácio acid test = (ativos correntes − inventário) ÷ passivos correntes = 9,000 ÷ 6,000 = 1.5

O acid test retira o inventário porque o stock pode ser difícil de vender depressa. Uma orientação comum é 1.5 a 2 para o rácio de liquidez corrente e cerca de 1 para o acid test. Isto varia conforme o setor.

keyPoints: Um balanço mostra a posição numa data.
Ativos = capital + passivos.
Fundo de maneio = ativos correntes − passivos correntes.
Rácio de liquidez corrente = ativos correntes ÷ passivos correntes.
Acid test = (ativos correntes − inventário) ÷ passivos correntes.

es.title: El balance de situación y los ratios de liquidez
es.short: Activos, pasivos y capital, capital circulante, y los ratios de liquidez corriente y de prueba ácida.

sections.heading: Qué muestra
sections.text:
Un balance de situación (balance sheet), también llamado estado de situación financiera, muestra lo que una empresa posee y lo que debe en una fecha determinada.

Los activos son cosas que posee la empresa. Los activos no corrientes se conservan durante más de un año, como los edificios y las máquinas. Los activos corrientes probablemente se conviertan en efectivo en menos de un año, como el inventario, el efectivo y las cuentas por cobrar. Las cuentas por cobrar son el dinero que deben los clientes.

Los pasivos son deudas. Los pasivos corrientes deben pagarse en menos de un año, como el dinero que se debe a los proveedores. Los pasivos no corrientes son a largo plazo, como un préstamo a cinco años.

El capital, o patrimonio neto, es el dinero de los propietarios en la empresa.

Los dos lados deben ser siempre iguales:
Activos = capital + pasivos

sections.heading: Un ejemplo resuelto
sections.text:
Una empresa comercial nigeriana tiene estos saldos, en nairas.
Activos no corrientes: 40,000
Inventario: 6,000
Cuentas por cobrar: 5,000
Efectivo: 4,000
Pasivos corrientes: 6,000
Pasivos no corrientes: 9,000
Capital: 40,000

Activos corrientes = 6,000 + 5,000 + 4,000 = 15,000
Activos totales = 40,000 + 15,000 = 55,000
Capital + pasivos = 40,000 + 6,000 + 9,000 = 55,000
Los dos lados cuadran.

sections.heading: Medir la liquidez
sections.text:
La liquidez es la capacidad de pagar las deudas a corto plazo.
Capital circulante = activos corrientes − pasivos corrientes = 15,000 − 6,000 = 9,000
Ratio de liquidez corriente = activos corrientes ÷ pasivos corrientes = 15,000 ÷ 6,000 = 2.5
Ratio de prueba ácida = (activos corrientes − inventario) ÷ pasivos corrientes = 9,000 ÷ 6,000 = 1.5

La prueba ácida excluye el inventario porque las existencias pueden ser difíciles de vender rápidamente. Una orientación habitual es de 1.5 a 2 para el ratio de liquidez corriente y de alrededor de 1 para la prueba ácida. Esto varía según el sector.

keyPoints: Un balance de situación muestra la posición en una fecha determinada.
Activos = capital + pasivos.
Capital circulante = activos corrientes − pasivos corrientes.
Ratio de liquidez corriente = activos corrientes ÷ pasivos corrientes.
Prueba ácida = (activos corrientes − inventario) ÷ pasivos corrientes.

yo.title: Balance sheet àti liquidity ratios
yo.short: Assets, liabilities àti capital, working capital, àti current ratio àti acid test ratio.
keywords: ìwé ohun tí a ní àti gbèsè tí a jẹ

sections.heading: Ohun tó ń fi hàn
sections.text:
Balance sheet, tí a tún ń pè ní statement of financial position, ń fi ohun tí iṣẹ́ òwò ní àti gbèsè tó jẹ hàn ní ọjọ́ kan.

Assets ni àwọn ohun tí iṣẹ́ òwò ní. Non-current assets ni a máa ń pa mọ́ fún ju ọdún kan lọ, bíi ilé àti ẹ̀rọ. Current assets ni ó ṣeé ṣe kí wọ́n di owó lọ́wọ́ láàárín ọdún kan, bíi inventory (ọjà tó wà nílẹ̀), cash (owó lọ́wọ́) àti receivables. Receivables ni owó tí àwọn oníbàárà jẹ iṣẹ́ òwò náà.

Liabilities ni àwọn gbèsè. A gbọ́dọ̀ san current liabilities láàárín ọdún kan, bíi owó tí a jẹ àwọn supplier (àwọn tó ń pèsè ọjà). Non-current liabilities jẹ́ ti ìgbà pípẹ́, bíi loan ọdún márùn-ún.

Capital, tàbí equity, ni owó àwọn olóhun nínú iṣẹ́ òwò.

Àwọn ẹ̀gbẹ́ méjèèjì gbọ́dọ̀ dọ́gba nígbà gbogbo:
Assets = capital + liabilities

sections.heading: Àpẹẹrẹ ìṣirò
sections.text:
Ilé-iṣẹ́ òwò kan ní Nàìjíríà ní àwọn iye wọ̀nyí, ní naira.
Non-current assets: 40,000
Inventory: 6,000
Receivables: 5,000
Cash: 4,000
Current liabilities: 6,000
Non-current liabilities: 9,000
Capital: 40,000

Current assets = 6,000 + 5,000 + 4,000 = 15,000
Total assets = 40,000 + 15,000 = 55,000
Capital + liabilities = 40,000 + 6,000 + 9,000 = 55,000
Àwọn ẹ̀gbẹ́ méjèèjì dọ́gba.

sections.heading: Wíwọn liquidity
sections.text:
Liquidity ni agbára láti san àwọn gbèsè ìgbà kúkúrú.
Working capital = current assets − current liabilities = 15,000 − 6,000 = 9,000
Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities = 15,000 ÷ 6,000 = 2.5
Acid test ratio = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities = 9,000 ÷ 6,000 = 1.5

Acid test yọ inventory kúrò nítorí pé ó lè ṣòro láti ta stock kíákíá. Ìtọ́sọ́nà kan tó wọ́pọ̀ ni 1.5 sí 2 fún current ratio àti nǹkan bíi 1 fún acid test. Èyí yàtọ̀ láti industry (irú iṣẹ́ òwò) kan sí òmíràn.

keyPoints: Balance sheet ń fi ipò iṣẹ́ òwò hàn ní ọjọ́ kan.
Assets = capital + liabilities.
Working capital = current assets − current liabilities.
Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities.
Acid test = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities.

ig.title: Balance sheet na liquidity ratios
ig.short: Assets, liabilities na capital, working capital, na current ratio na acid test ratio.

sections.heading: Ihe ọ na-egosi
sections.text:
Balance sheet, nke a na-akpọkwa statement of financial position, na-egosi ihe azụmahịa nwere na ihe ọ ji n’ụgwọ n’otu ụbọchị.

Assets bụ ihe azụmahịa nwere. A na-edebe non-current assets karịa otu afọ, dị ka ụlọ na igwe. O yiri ka current assets ga-aghọ ego n’aka n’ime otu afọ, dị ka inventory (stock), ego n’aka na receivables. Receivables bụ ego ndị ahịa ji.

Liabilities bụ ụgwọ azụmahịa ji (debts). A ga-akwụrịrị current liabilities n’ime otu afọ, dị ka ego azụmahịa ji ndị na-eweta ihe n’ụgwọ. Non-current liabilities bụ nke ogologo oge, dị ka ego e gbaziri nke afọ ise.

Capital, ma ọ bụ equity, bụ ego ndị nwe ya n’azụmahịa ahụ.

Akụkụ abụọ ahụ ga-aharịrị nhata mgbe niile:
Assets = capital + liabilities

sections.heading: Ihe atụ e gbakọrọ
sections.text:
Otu ụlọ ọrụ trade na Nigeria nwere balances ndị a, na naira.
Non-current assets: 40,000
Inventory: 6,000
Receivables: 5,000
Ego n’aka: 4,000
Current liabilities: 6,000
Non-current liabilities: 9,000
Capital: 40,000

Current assets = 6,000 + 5,000 + 4,000 = 15,000
Total assets = 40,000 + 15,000 = 55,000
Capital + liabilities = 40,000 + 6,000 + 9,000 = 55,000
Akụkụ abụọ ahụ hara nhata.

sections.heading: Ịtụ liquidity
sections.text:
Liquidity bụ ikike ịkwụ ụgwọ a ga-akwụ n’ime obere oge (short-term debts).
Working capital = current assets − current liabilities = 15,000 − 6,000 = 9,000
Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities = 15,000 ÷ 6,000 = 2.5
Acid test ratio = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities = 9,000 ÷ 6,000 = 1.5

Acid test na-ewepụ inventory n’ihi na stock nwere ike isi ike ire ngwa ngwa. Ihe nduzi a na-ejikarị bụ 1.5 ruo 2 maka current ratio na ihe dị ka 1 maka acid test. Nke a dị iche site n’otu ụdị ụlọ ọrụ (industry) gaa n’ọzọ.

keyPoints: Balance sheet na-egosi ọnọdụ n’otu ụbọchị.
Assets = capital + liabilities.
Working capital = current assets − current liabilities.
Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities.
Acid test = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities.

ha.title: Balance sheet da liquidity ratios
ha.short: Assets, liabilities da capital, working capital, da current da acid test ratios.

sections.heading: Abin da yake nunawa
sections.text:
Balance sheet, wanda ake kuma kira statement of financial position, yana nuna abin da kasuwanci ya mallaka da bashin da ake bin sa a wata rana ɗaya.

Assets (kadarori) abubuwa ne da kasuwanci ya mallaka. Non-current assets ana riƙe su fiye da shekara ɗaya, kamar gine-gine da na’urori. Current assets ana sa ran za su zama kuɗin hannu (cash) a cikin shekara ɗaya, kamar inventory, kuɗin hannu da receivables. Receivables su ne kuɗin da kasuwanci yake bin abokan ciniki.

Liabilities (basussuka) su ne bashin da ake bin kasuwanci. Dole a biya current liabilities a cikin shekara ɗaya, kamar kuɗin da masu kawo kaya suke bin kasuwanci. Non-current liabilities na dogon lokaci ne, kamar rance na shekara biyar.

Capital, ko equity, shi ne kuɗin masu kasuwanci a cikin kasuwancin.

Dole ɓangarorin biyu su kasance daidai ko da yaushe:
Assets = capital + liabilities

sections.heading: Misalin lissafi
sections.text:
Wani kamfanin ciniki na Najeriya yana da waɗannan adadi, a naira.
Non-current assets: 40,000
Inventory: 6,000
Receivables: 5,000
Kuɗin hannu (cash): 4,000
Current liabilities: 6,000
Non-current liabilities: 9,000
Capital: 40,000

Current assets = 6,000 + 5,000 + 4,000 = 15,000
Jimillar assets = 40,000 + 15,000 = 55,000
Capital + liabilities = 40,000 + 6,000 + 9,000 = 55,000
Ɓangarorin biyu sun daidaita.

sections.heading: Auna liquidity
sections.text:
Liquidity ita ce ikon biyan basussukan ɗan gajeren lokaci.
Working capital = current assets − current liabilities = 15,000 − 6,000 = 9,000
Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities = 15,000 ÷ 6,000 = 2.5
Acid test ratio = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities = 9,000 ÷ 6,000 = 1.5

Acid test yana cire inventory domin stock na iya zama da wuyar sayarwa da sauri. Jagorar da aka saba amfani da ita ita ce 1.5 zuwa 2 ga current ratio da kusan 1 ga acid test. Wannan yana bambanta bisa irin masana’antu.

keyPoints: Balance sheet yana nuna matsayin kasuwanci a wata rana ɗaya.
Assets = capital + liabilities.
Working capital = current assets − current liabilities.
Current ratio = current assets ÷ current liabilities.
Acid test = (current assets − inventory) ÷ current liabilities.

en.title: Cash flow
en.short: Why cash is different from profit, how to read a cash flow forecast and how to fix shortages.

sections.heading: Cash is not profit
sections.text:
Cash flow is the movement of money into and out of a business. Inflows include cash sales, money from customers who bought on credit, and loans. Outflows include wages, rent and payments to suppliers.

A sale made on credit counts as revenue when it is made, yet the cash may arrive months later. So a business can be profitable but have no cash to pay its bills. Many businesses fail for this reason.

sections.heading: A cash flow forecast
sections.text:
A forecast estimates future cash flows, usually month by month. It helps owners see shortages early and it can support a bank loan request.

Net cash flow = inflows − outflows
Closing balance = opening balance + net cash flow
The closing balance of one month is the opening balance of the next.

Example in naira:
Month 1: opening 5,000; in 20,000; out 22,000; net −2,000; closing 3,000
Month 2: opening 3,000; in 18,000; out 24,000; net −6,000; closing −3,000
Month 3: opening −3,000; in 30,000; out 23,000; net +7,000; closing 4,000

The business is short of cash in month 2, so it may arrange an overdraft before this happens. A forecast is only an estimate, because sales and costs can change.

sections.heading: Fixing a shortage
sections.text:
To improve cash flow, a business can:
Ask customers to pay sooner, or offer a discount for quick payment.
Ask suppliers for more time to pay.
Arrange an overdraft or a short-term loan.
Hold less stock.
Sell unused assets.
Delay spending that is not urgent.

Each choice has a cost. Customers may leave if asked to pay too quickly, and suppliers may refuse more credit.

keyPoints: Cash flow is the movement of money in and out.
Profit is not the same as cash.
Net cash flow = inflows − outflows.
Closing balance = opening balance + net cash flow.
A profitable business can still fail from lack of cash.

pcm.title: Cash flow
pcm.short: Why cash different from profit, how to read cash flow forecast and how to fix shortages.

sections.text:
